trust_decision.summary: Atomics builtins decide that the typed-array byte position is in bounds of a live (non-detached) buffer once, in validateAtomicAccess, before running user-controlled coercions (ToIndex/ToInteger/ToBigInt valueOf) that can detach or shrink the ArrayBuffer; the raw buffer access afterwards trusts that stale decision, and the low-level getValueFromBuffer/setValueInBuffer only ASSERT bounds (debug-only).

landing_point.why: A TOCTOU in Atomics leads straight to atomicReadModifyWrite, the shared helper behind add/and/or/sub/xor/exchange, where the value coercion runs after the bounds check.

fix_sites.entry_point: ArrayBufferObject::getValueFromBuffer (lower-level runtime API used by Atomics.load, TypedArray element get, DataView get, TypedArray builtins)
ArrayBufferObject::setValueInBuffer (lower-level runtime API used by Atomics.store, TypedArray element set, DataView set, TypedArray builtins)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/runtime/ArrayBufferObject.cpp:183-217 (getValueFromBuffer/setValueInBuffer: ASSERT-only checks turned into runtime TypeError/RangeError)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The runtime getValueFromBuffer/setValueInBuffer are generic helpers whose callers (DataView, TypedArray element get/set, copyWithin, slice) already check detach/bounds after coercion, so a solver can argue the ASSERTs are a valid caller contract and only the Atomics callers are buggy; conversely a solver who hardens only these helpers misses add/sub/and/or/xor/exchange and compareExchange, which bypass them and write through buffer->data() directly.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Atomics on a SharedArrayBuffer, or on a resizable ArrayBuffer that a valueOf grows or leaves alone, must keep succeeding, and the spec order (coerce index, then value, then re-check) must hold; checking detach before coercion, or rejecting length-tracking/resizable views outright, breaks legitimate calls. TypedArray element set on a detached buffer must still silently return true rather than throw.

O6_input_shapes: Number-typed integer arrays (Int8/16/32, Uint8/16/32) with value coerced via ToInteger
BigInt64/BigUint64 arrays with value coerced via ToBigInt
index coercion (ToIndex valueOf) as the trigger, which covers Atomics.load with no value argument
compareExchange with two coerced operands (expected and replacement)
buffer detached (ArrayBuffer.prototype.transfer/transferToFixedLength) vs. resizable buffer shrunk via resize()

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Atomics.notify coerces count (toInteger) after validateAtomicAccess, then derives an address from buffer->data(); a variant that reads or writes the slot after the count coercion would be a direct sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: notify already follows the same validate-then-coerce order; a maintainer adding a debug read or a non-shared fast path would reuse the stale indexedPosition.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: doWait coerces value and timeout after validateAtomicAccess and then calls getValueFromBuffer; if the SharedArrayBuffer-only check at :335 were relaxed (e.g. waitAsync on non-shared buffers), it becomes a second TOCTOU route.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Engines have debated allowing wait on non-shared buffers; moving or dropping the isSharedArrayBufferObject check is a plausible refactor.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The SharedArrayBufferObject second implementation of getValueFromBuffer/setValueInBuffer keeps ASSERT-only bounds checks (:155-157, :228-230) that the fix did not harden.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is a parallel override of the patched function in another file; a planted shrinkable or detachable path there would pass review easily.

O9_family: TOCTOU / stale bounds check after user-code coercion leading to out-of-bounds memory access on a detached or shrunk ArrayBuffer (CWE-367 -> memory safety)

O10_build.toolchain: CMake + GCC/Clang; Atomics is compiled only with ESCARGOT_THREADING (-DENABLE_THREADING, build/config.cmake:148-149); bundled bdwgc in third_party
O10_build.project_tests: test/vendortest submodule (test262 and others); the fix only bumps the submodule pointer (fix.diff:118-124), so regression tests sit in the vendortest repo, not in this tree

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a re-check only in atomicReadModifyWrite, or only harden ArrayBufferObject::getValueFromBuffer/setValueInBuffer, missing compareExchange and the RMW ops that write through buffer->data() directly (src/builtins/BuiltinAtomics.cpp:143, :225).

out_of_scope_notes: Atomics.notify and doWait compute an address as int32_t* + byte position (src/builtins/BuiltinAtomics.cpp:374, :532), scaling the byte index by 4; it is only used as a waiter-list key, not dereferenced, so it is not this advisory's flaw.
